# Attachment owner routing

Regenerate with `python3 -B scripts/build_eapdf_attachment_owner_fixtures.py`.
The retained _source.pdf was generated by the accepted unchanged creator from
two synthetic EMLs. Their identifiers differ in the local part: Owner@example.org
and owner@example.org. Only the first email has an attachment. The source
inputs, command and generator log are retained in docs/improvement/validator-17.
The mutation recipe preserves the archive, source streams and payloads and uses
deterministic serialization IDs.

Table 19 permits Message-ID-only attachment identity. Resolve it to a unique
email XMP record, preserving identifier case/punctuation, then route through
that email's required GUID to body DPM. Table 7 makes DPM Mail_MessageID
optional. A supplied attachment GUID retains priority. Ambiguous or missing XMP
owners remain unavailable; the tests do not claim general RFC canonicalization
or global attachment occurrence assignment.

Five positives pass: unchanged GUID, Message-ID-only, optional DPM IDs omitted,
Message-ID-only with a permitted native filename alias/no optional checksum, and a source-omitted control.
Two wrong-owner controls fail: an attachment attributed to the other email
fails ATTACHMENT_XMP_MATCH, ATTACHMENT_ANNOTATIONS_PRESENT and MESSAGE_ATTACHMENT_COUNT_XMP; a correct GUID
with a contradictory Message-ID fails ATTACHMENT_XMP_MATCH. Two more source-omitted cases fail MESSAGE_ATTACHMENT_COUNT_XMP when the count is missing or zero. Ownership proves only that the count must be positive; it does not prove the exact total. Independent before/after results are retained with the evidence.
